requirements.title: Computer Science minor eligibility
requirements.summary: Students may not pursue more than one CS minor. CS majors may pursue only the computational biology/bioinformatics minor, so are not eligible for this AI minor.

requirements.title: Trinity minor policy
requirements.summary: A minor requires at least five courses, at least half in Duke course credits. Majors, minors and certificates together may total at most three. General policy permits major/minor overlap unless the program restricts it; it prohibits a same-department major/minor except named exceptions. Use the registrar academic-plan change process for adding/changing a minor.

requirements.title: D grades and credential requirements
requirements.summary: The bulletin treats D as a low pass that can satisfy other requirements, while limiting D-graded courses to two toward continuation and the 34-course-credit host degree total. This is a general policy, not an invented minimum AI-course grade.

requirements.title: S/U grading for program requirements
requirements.summary: A voluntarily S/U-graded course cannot satisfy major, minor or certificate requirements, including prerequisites, without the program DUS permission. S requires work equivalent to C- or better; U gives no credit. This exception requires individual approval, not automatic eligibility.

requirements.title: Entrance credit is subject to department acceptance
requirements.summary: AP, IPC and prematriculation college credit may meet departmental major/minor requirements only to the extent permitted by that department. Prematriculation coursework must meet the published conditions, including B- or better and exclusion of work used for the high-school diploma; acceptance is not inferred for any listed AI course.

requirements.title: Incoming transfer approval and local coursework
requirements.summary: For students transferring into Duke, the academic unit must approve transfer courses toward the major/minor/certificate. At least half of each credential must be completed at Duke. This college/school-specific evaluation rule is separate from host-degree residency.

requirements.title: Post-matriculation transfer approval
requirements.summary: Individually arranged transfer courses require advance approval from the subject DUS and appropriate dean, followed by completion and final official transcript review. Limits are two such courses for Trinity students and four for Pratt students; academic-dismissal transfers are limited to two within those totals.

requirements.title: Study-away transfer limits and approval
requirements.summary: GEO-facilitated study away permits up to four credits per semester or eight per year, potentially two more for summer; combined study-away and individually arranged transfers cannot exceed ten courses. Pratt transfers may include at most two engineering courses. Relevant DUS approval, GEO arrangements and final transcript review are required; non-Duke summer programs require GEO approval.

requirements.title: Transfer grading and credit equivalence
requirements.summary: Post-matriculation transfer courses require C- or better; P/F or equivalent grades are ineligible. The Registrar determines credit equivalence; Duke course credits are not assumed equivalent to semester or quarter hours. Transfer grades do not enter the Duke record/GPA, and work beyond the transfer limit cannot replace an earlier transfer course.

requirements.title: Trinity S/U approvals and course eligibility
requirements.summary: For Trinity students, the program must permit S/U credit toward its requirements. A course must permit voluntary S/U; courses numbered 500 or higher additionally require instructor permission. Only one voluntary S/U course credit per semester or summer term may be requested, by the withdrawal deadline; the change cannot be reversed. This is not automatic permission for any AI course.

requirements.title: Trinity individually arranged transfer-course conditions
requirements.summary: In addition to department acceptance and prior Dean/DUS approval, individually arranged transfer courses cannot coincide with Duke enrollment, including online Duke courses. Community/junior college work after Duke matriculation is ineligible. Summer courses require at least four weeks and 17 class meetings. A course previously passed at Duke with D-/D/D+ cannot receive replacement transfer credit. Overseas institutional accreditation must be confirmed; third-party transcript arrangements are ineligible. These conditions apply to Trinity students and do not import its general-education curriculum into this credential.
